overview: North Macedonia is a landlocked country in the Balkans. Its capital and largest city is Skopje. It became independent from Yugoslavia in 1991, and in 2019 it changed its name from Macedonia to North Macedonia after an agreement with Greece. It joined NATO in 2020.

geography.text: North Macedonia is mostly mountainous, cut through by the valley of the Vardar, its main river, which flows south into Greece. In the south-west it shares two large lakes with its neighbours: Lake Ohrid with Albania, and Lake Prespa with Albania and Greece. Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe.

history.text: The region was the heartland of ancient Macedon, then part of the Roman and Byzantine empires, and was ruled by the Ottomans for about 500 years. After the Balkan Wars it became part of Serbia and then Yugoslavia. It became independent in 1991, and a long naming dispute with Greece was settled with an agreement in 2018, leading to its new name, North Macedonia, in 2019.

events.title: Balkan Wars
events.text: The region of Macedonia is divided between its neighbours.

events.title: New name

events.title: Joins NATO
events.text: North Macedonia becomes a member of NATO.

government.text: North Macedonia is a parliamentary republic. Its parliament, the Sobranie, chooses the Prime Minister, and the President is elected directly. The country changed its name from Macedonia to North Macedonia in 2019 under an agreement with Greece, which opened the way for it to join NATO in 2020. It is a candidate to join the European Union.

economy.text: North Macedonia's economy includes farming, especially tobacco, wine and vegetables, mining, textiles and car parts made by foreign companies in special economic zones. Many people work abroad and send money home.

culture.text: Lake Ohrid, one of the oldest lakes in the world, is lined with Byzantine churches and monasteries. Macedonian is a South Slavic language written in Cyrillic, and about a quarter of the population is Albanian. Mother Teresa was born in Skopje in 1910.

items.title: Lake Ohrid
items.text: More than a million years old, shared with Albania.

items.title: Mother Teresa
items.text: Born in Skopje to an Albanian family.

sport.text: Handball and basketball are very popular in North Macedonia, and club handball side Vardar Skopje has twice been champion of Europe. The footballer Goran Pandev won the Champions League with Inter Milan in 2010.

items.title: Euro 2020
items.text: North Macedonia's first major men's football tournament.

items.title: Handball
items.text: Club Vardar Skopje won the EHF Champions League in 2017 and 2019.

didYouKnow: Lake Ohrid is thought to be more than a million years old.
North Macedonia's flag shows a golden sun with eight rays.
